samples.reason: The task requires both creative generation (designing a novel number theory worksheet) and rigorous mathematical reasoning (constructing a valid Pythagorean analogy, verifying clean factorization, and executing the extended Euclidean algorithm correctly). Dunlin significantly outperforms Willet on Arena-Hard (90.6 vs. 83.2) and GPQA Diamond (64.1 vs. 56.2), indicating stronger reasoning and instruction-following for complex technical content, while its Creative Generation score is at least equivalent (difference is at the 2.0-point tie threshold). This makes it the better choice for producing a clean, accurate, and pedagogically useful worked example.

The query requires designing a novel number-theory problem from scratch, solving it with correct Euclidean-algorithm steps, and presenting the solution clearly—spanning creative generation, mathematical reasoning, and structured exposition. Dunlin-235B outperforms Willet-235B on Creative Generation and dominates on every other internal eval dimension (Extraction & Retrieval, Summarization, Support Dialogue, and Policy & Moderation), making it the more capable choice for this open-ended yet precision-sensitive task.

Dunlin scores higher on Creative Generation (84.7 vs. 82.7) and substantially higher on the structured explanatory categories relevant here—Summarization (86.4 vs. 80.6) and Support Dialogue (83.9 vs. 78.9)—making it the better fit for producing a clean, worked worksheet solution.
